beats: You are not exhausted because your life is hard. You are exhausted because you care about too many useless things.

HOOK SCENE WITH BOOK COVER: Extreme visual contrast. In the center, the stickman stands at a stark fork in a sandy road, scratching his messy spiky hair in deep existential confusion. To his left, a curved golden treadmill surrounded by swirling green dollar bills and a glittering trophy; to his right, a steep rugged black mountain trail ascending toward a warm smiling yellow cartoon sun. In the bottom-right corner rests a crisp, vibrant orange book cover with bold black block letters: 'THE SUBTLE ART OF NOT GIVING A F*CK by Mark Manson' with clean drop shadow. At the top center, handwritten black font reads: 'Why You Care Too Much'. Generous white negative space, bold ink lines.
Every single day, society bombards you with one relentless, toxic lie: be richer, be happier, be perfect.

SOCIETY'S SENSORY BOMBARDMENT: The stickman is pinned to the floor in the center, hands shielding his face in visceral sensory overload. Looming over him are giant menacing billboard screens with aggressive electric-cyan and crimson glowing slogans: 'BE RICHER', 'LOOK BETTER', 'BUY MORE'. Jagged red lightning bolts and blaring loudspeaker megaphones beam directly down into his trembling skull. Droplets of cold cyan sweat fly through the air.

THE GREED TRAP: A panicked stickman is perched precariously on top of an insanely tall, wobbling pyramid of gold coins that is teetering on the verge of collapsing. Gold coins are slipping beneath his trembling feet. His eyes are wide with terrified paranoia as he desperately juggles floating dollar signs, unable to enjoy a single cent.

THE FAKE SMILE MASK: High emotional pathos. The stickman stands slumped in front of a mirror with bruised weary eyes and an exhausted frown. With trembling hands, he straps a giant, garish yellow ceramic smiley face mask over his real face with visible brown duct tape, faking joy while his soul is drained.

TOXIC POSITIVITY STRAIN: The stickman is forced into an aggressive double thumbs-up pose with a manic gritted-teeth smile. Blinding neon electric-yellow sparkles and giant cartoon badges labeled 'GOOD VIBES ONLY' buzz violently around his head, while his eye twitches in agonizing comic tension.
And when you feel anxious, you get anxious about being anxious.

SPIRALING ANXIETY CLONES: The stickman is huddled on a cold stone bench with his head clutched between white-knuckled hands. Floating in an escalating orbit around him are four translucent phantom clones of himself, each biting their nails with wide bloodshot cartoon eyes, whispering spiraling thoughts directly into his ears.
When you feel guilty, you feel guilty about feeling guilty.

THE GUILT GRAVITATIONAL CRUSH: The stickman is crushed flat against the stark white floor beneath the immense gravitational weight of a massive jagged black iron boulder strapped to his spine, with chains dragging in the dust. Dark shadow cracks radiate outward across the floor as he groans in suffocating self-blame.
Welcome to the feedback loop from hell.

THE FEEDBACK LOOP FROM HELL: Dramatic cinematic metaphor. The stickman is trapped at the dead center of a roaring circular ouroboros vortex made of searing crimson fire and thick black looping arrows labeled 'ANXIETY' -> 'PANIC' -> 'GUILT' -> 'SHAME'. Jagged red exclamation points explode in an infinite loop around him as he screams with his hands on his face.
Conventional self-help tells you to look in the mirror and scream affirmations.

DELUSIONAL MIRROR SCREAMING: The stickman stands in an exaggerated martial arts power stance inches away from an ornate gold-framed mirror, veins bulging on his throat, screaming affirmations so violently that spit particles fly and his reflection’s hair is blown backward by the shockwave.
To care deeply about every single little thing.

OVERWHELMED PLATE JUGGLING: The stickman is balanced on one foot, sweating cyan fountains, frantically juggling eight fragile ceramic plates labeled 'Career', 'Abs', 'Followers', 'E-mails', 'Status', 'Gossip'. Several plates are already cracking in mid-air and wobbling violently.
To believe you are special, entitled to a frictionless, pain-free life.

THE FRAGILE ENTITLEMENT THRONE: The stickman sits pompously on a wobbly tower of soggy cardboard boxes, wearing an absurdly crooked oversized golden paper burger crown. He has his arms crossed with an offended pout, snapping his fingers and expecting red velvet carpets to unroll beneath his feet.
This path is a deadly psychological trap.

THE RED CARPET TRAPDOOR: Wide dramatic shot. A glossy red carpet pathway leads straight toward a bottomless black pitfall lined with razor-sharp black stone spikes. Above the pit hangs a giant swinging cartoon guillotine blade labeled 'DISAPPOINTMENT'. The stickman's shoe is hovering inches over the edge.
The desire for more positive experience is itself a negative experience.

CHASING THE GOLDEN BUTTERFLY MIRAGE: The stickman is sprinting on a cracked desert treadmill, tongue dangling out in utter dehydration, reaching forward with desperate scraped hands toward a radiant golden butterfly that flutters just two inches beyond his fingertips. The faster he runs, the hotter the floor burns.
And the acceptance of one's negative experience is itself a positive experience.

RADICAL ACCEPTANCE RAIN ZEN: High emotional contrast. A violent downpour of dark rain lashes the scene, but the stickman stands completely serene beneath a sturdy emerald-green umbrella. His eyes are gently closed with a peaceful, knowing smile, hands tucked comfortably in his pockets as raindrops bounce harmlessly off the canvas into a flowering green cactus.
Wait! Not giving a fuck does NOT mean being indifferent or callous.

THE MID-VIDEO REHOOK: A giant red 'HALT / CAUTION' barrier slams down between the viewer and the stickman. The stickman steps through with an assertive, serious gaze, holding up one hand to stop the viewer. Contrasted beside him is an icy blue stone statue with dead hollow eyes, showing what apathy actually looks like.
A person who is indifferent isn't cool. They are terrified of the world.

THE BUNKER COWARD: A pathetic, shivering stick figure is curled up inside a dark grey reinforced concrete bunker wrapped in thick steel chains and padlocks. He peeks out of a tiny slit with gigantic, trembling cartoon eyes, terrified of a gentle sunny breeze and singing birds in the outside world.
Not giving a fuck means being comfortable with being different.

WALKING AGAINST THE HERD: An entire gray army of identical, faceless stick figures march in mindless unison toward the left into a dull fog. In vivid contrast, our protagonist with messy black hair and a vibrant terracotta shirt walks with relaxed stride and confident posture to the right, totally unbothered by their stares.
It means realizing that your fucks are strictly finite.

THE FINITE FUCKS JAR: Close-up on the stickman holding a heavy crystal jar labeled 'FUCKS TO GIVE'. Through the transparent glass, only THREE glowing, radiant golden coins remain at the very bottom. He gazes at the coins with solemn, guarded reverence, knowing once they're spent, they're gone forever.
If you give a fuck about your broken Wi-Fi,

THE OVERHEATED ROUTER RAGE: Comedic relatable rage. The stickman violently shakes a smoking black internet router emitting red spark flashes and a frozen 99% loading spinner. Veins throb on his forehead, his hair stands on end, and steam whistles from his cartoon ears.

THE CAFE SLAM: A scowling, grumpy barista with crossed arms and an apron aggressively slams a ceramic mug of hot coffee onto the wooden counter, splashing brown coffee onto the counter with an explosive splash starburst.

GOSSIP SHADOW DARTS: Dark lurking silhouettes in the background whispering with sharp black gossip speech bubbles that shoot tiny harmless dart arrows toward the stickman, which bounce off his invisible barrier and shatter into dust on the floor.
you run out of fucks for what actually matters.

THE EMPTY JAR HEARTBREAK: Visceral emotional gut-punch. The stickman drops to his knees staring in despair at his shattered glass jar, completely empty with zero golden coins. In the blurred background, an unfinished oil painting, an unread book, and a crying partner sit ignored in the shadows.
It all comes down to your values.

THE ANCIENT VALUE ARCHES: Grand compositional framing. The stickman stands at the foot of two towering stone monuments carved into desert bedrock: the left arch is cracked crumbling sandstone labeled 'BAD VALUES'; the right arch is polished emerald-green granite labeled 'GOOD VALUES'.
Bad values are external, superficial, and uncontrollable:

CATCHING SLIPPERY SMOKE: The stickman desperately tries to wrap his arms around swirling black smoke clouds and falling desert sand that effortlessly slip through his open fingers, leaving his hands dirty and empty.

HEDONIC BURNOUT COMA: The stickman is melted like liquid into a greasy beanbag chair, surrounded by piles of discarded junk food wrappers, energy drink cans, and a blinding blue smartphone screen. His eyes are glazed, totally numb, dead inside from endless dopamine chasing.

THE CRACKING SPORTS CAR: A vain stick figure wearing oversized sunglasses poses smugly against a flashy red supercar, but a huge jagged fracture runs down the entire vehicle, exposing hollow cardboard and duct tape inside.
and always having to be right.

THE LONELY LECTERN: A red-faced stick figure shouts violently through a megaphone behind a wooden podium, pointing an angry accusatory finger into an empty void while all his former friends walk away into the distance, leaving him utterly alone.
Good values are internal and controllable: honesty, humility, curiosity, and self-respect.

THE UNBREAKABLE EMERALD PILLAR: The stickman stands calm and composed with his back resting against a massive emerald-green pillar rooted hundreds of feet into bedrock. Fierce windstorms and dust whirlwinds blow violently around him, but the pillar and the stickman do not budge a single millimeter.

AUTHENTIC VULNERABILITY: Two stick figures sit across a simple wooden table sharing hot steaming tea. Both have their palms resting open on the table, looking directly into each other's eyes with warm, relaxed smiles of mutual trust and zero pretension.

STARGAZER TELESCOPE: Nighttime aesthetic on white canvas. The stickman gazes with childlike wonder through an antique brass telescope pointed up at a cluster of brilliant golden stars, holding an open notebook with quiet inner pride.
Stop asking what success you want. Ask what pain you are willing to sustain.

PUSHING ASIDE THE HOLLOW TROPHY: With a firm, decisive hand, the stickman shoves a glittering golden trophy off a pedestal, watching it smash to pieces on the floor, while his eyes lock onto a heavy craftsman hammer and workbench.
Because the struggle is where meaning lives.

LACING THE HIKING BOOTS: Close-up on the stickman kneeling on red dirt rock, vigorously pulling the leather laces tight on heavy mud-caked hiking boots. Sleeves rolled up, beads of honest sweat on his brow, looking up at a menacing rocky mountain peak with a fierce, hungry grin.
Happiness is not an equation you solve once.

ERASING THE COMPLEX FORMULA: A giant classroom blackboard covered in crazy, impossible math equations and stress formulas is being violently wiped clean with a giant wet sponge by the stickman, leaving pure, peaceful black slate.
Happiness comes from actively solving problems.

THE WATER VALVE TRIUMPH: The stickman wipes his brow with a greasy cloth, holding a heavy cartoon pipe wrench with a victorious beam. Behind him, clean sparkling blue water flows smoothly from a once-burst pipe into a lush blooming desert garden.
When you upgrade your values, you upgrade the quality of your problems.

UPGRADING YOUR PROBLEMS: Split vertical screen. Top half shows stick figures having a hysterical, screaming brawl over a dropped piece of candy; bottom half shows a focused stickman team sweating together to raise the heavy timber roof beam of a community shelter.
And when you feel completely stuck, remember the Do Something Principle.

FROZEN IN PARALYSIS MUD: The stickman is stuck waist-deep in thick gray quicksand, arms trembling with analysis paralysis. Floating above his head is a golden clockwork mechanism with three interlocking gears: [ACTION] -> [INSPIRATION] -> [MOTIVATION].
Action is not just the result of motivation.

THE COBWEB BENCH: A tragic stick figure sits frozen on a wooden park bench, arms limp, completely covered in thick spiderwebs and dust, staring at the sky waiting for a mythical lightning bolt of inspiration that will never come.
Action is the CAUSE of motivation.

STRIKING THE FLINT SPARK: Dynamic close-up. The stickman strikes a sharp black flint stone against rough steel with sudden explosive force. A shower of brilliant golden sparks bursts across the frame, instantly igniting a warm, crackling campfire flame.
Do something small, and the momentum will follow.

THE BOULDER OF MOMENTUM: The stickman uses one finger to give a tiny push to a small round stone atop a hill. As it rolls, it instantly snowballs into a colossal, unstoppable boulder of kinetic energy that smashes straight through concrete barricades.
Here is the ultimate truth: you are going to die.

MEMENTO MORI CONTEMPLATION: Haunting, cinematic beauty. The stickman sits peacefully atop a solitary desert rock under a vast indigo night sky filled with twinkling stars. In both hands, he holds up a stylized minimalist cartoon skull, staring into its hollow eyes with calm, fearless acceptance of his mortality.
Confronting your mortality strips away all superficial noise.

THE PURIFYING HURRICANE: A massive gust of fresh wind sweeps across the frame. Flying away in the wind like dead autumn leaves are social media notification bells, fake trophies, gossiping masks, and dollar bills. The stickman stands rock-solid at the center, inhaling deeply with clear open lungs.

UNTOUCHABLE SERENITY: A swarm of annoying red cartoon mosquitoes labeled 'Critics', 'Drama', 'Trends' buzz frantically around the stickman, but he stands with hands in his pockets, serene and unbothered, smiling as they bounce off without leaving a mark.
So choose carefully what deserves your precious energy.

INVESTING IN THE SACRED HEARTH: Tender emotional close-up. The stickman gently places his last remaining radiant golden coins directly into the heart of a warm, comforting fireplace hearth where a steady golden flame warms his family and creative work.
Because what you give a fuck about is your life.

GRAND SUNRISE FINALE: Epic wide master shot. The stickman stands victorious on the jagged summit of a towering mountain peak at golden dawn. His hair and shirt billow in the wind, his arms are spread wide embracing the world, and a radiant smiling yellow sun bathes the entire pure white canvas in triumphant golden light.
